newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end down on profit taking, housing data.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end down on profit taking, housing data.

text.p: Profit taking following recent sharp gains and selling prompted by a bearish single-family home sales report kept CME lumber futures pressured at the close, traders said.

Futures showed early support on carryover fund buy stops in an expanded trading limit of $15.00 per tbf after two days of limit gains before slipping on profit taking and selling generated by the report, they said.
The Commerce Department reported October single-family new home sales down 8.7 percent to 714,000 units on a seasonally adjusted basis.

The October decline was the largest since March and fairly widespread across the country. September sales were also revised down, adding to the decline in sales. Economists had expected seasonally adjusted October home sales at 772,000 units.
Lumber closed $3.40 to $1.40 per thousand board feet lower with January off $2.90 at $399.30 and March off most at $385.30 per tbf.
